column1: # Game profile of DOOM 3 (Switch, update 1.0.5 = v327680). Plays on the Mac: new game into Mars City, lit and shadowed, at 60 fps
# id Software's id Tech 4 in its BFG Edition renderer (DOOM 3, Resurrection of Evil and The Lost Mission), SDK 14.3.0. It renders with NVIDIA's desktop OpenGL 4.5 through EGL (subsdk0,
# not loaded): main asks eglGetProcAddress for its GL functions, many by their ARB names, after checking a fixed list of extensions, and the host's GL layer implements them on
# Metal (dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m). Its game data is in id's .resources containers in the RomFS.
# The shaders are GLSL 1.50 its renderer makes at run time from the render programs in _common.resources (renderprogs/*.vertex / *.pixel), each the first time it is used: no game file
# holds them, so the NSP script captures them by booting the game on the Mac, where the capture run has the renderer convert every render program (dm/gfx/tools/idtech4_programs.py;
# gl_capture.tsv lists them), and dm/gfx/tools/gl_shaders.py translates them offline; the host finds each by the hash of its text

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk. subsdk0 is NVIDIA's OpenGL driver, which programs the GPU through NvRm: never loaded, the GL layer answers main's EGL and GL calls
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory; main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB, a 3328 MB heap region. The Mac footprint in Mars City
# no NVN shaders: the NVN tables stay empty (gl_shaders.py writes the GL library and its table, not the profile)

column2: DOOM 3 has no NVN shaders (its GLSL shaders go through the GL layer)
